prompt: From 'P → Q' and '¬P', what can you validly conclude?
options: Nothing, since this is denying the antecedent
hint: P → Q does not say P is the ONLY way to get Q. If P is false, is Q forced to be false?
explanation: Nothing follows. From P → Q and ¬P, concluding ¬Q denies the antecedent: Q can still be true another way. Modus tollens is the valid pattern: from P → Q and ¬Q, conclude ¬P.
